reason: Research this week (web search) confirms the theses of the core legs rather than challenging them: UnitedHealth beat Q3 on Oct 13 ($4.69 adj EPS vs ~$4.12) and raised 2026 guidance to at least $20.50, so the managed-care margin-recovery trade is working (UNH +7.5%, CI +9.9%); ExxonMobil reported $4.23 adjusted EPS on Oct 30 with record refining and ~$11B YTD net debt reduction, and Chevron printed $5.28 adjusted EPS with Brent still averaging $97, so the integrated-energy hedge (XOM +14.2%, CVX +14.1%) is intact in the oil-driven stagflation regime. ETH is a 3% legacy leg whose -20% stop will decide it, and selling it costs 35bps in friction for little risk reduction. The book is +20.7% with a -3.2% max drawdown, and cash is now about 26% after ACN hit its +30% take-profit on Oct 22. I am deliberately NOT redeploying that ACN cash this week: I could not verify Cigna's Q3 2026 print or research a fresh cheap-IT candidate thoroughly within the shared search budget, and adding a name from memory would be weaker than earning 4% on cash while the existing legs work. Trading for its own sake would only add churn.
